claim: Of the items in [61] that can replace if: “Assuming and supposing are verbs heading gerund-participial clauses.” The example is [62v], supposing (that) one were to waste money in that way.
evidence_summary: Ch. 11, p. 971 [58] lists supposing among the “Prepositions governing content clauses of this kind”, the expandable type that allows that, which is the construction of [62v]. Ch. 7, p. 611’s list of deverbal prepositions taking content clause complements (“given, granted, provided, providing, seeing”) omits supposing and considering.
finding: Medium-high confidence, for supposing only: Ch. 11 doesn’t list assuming. Ch. 7’s treatment of subjectless verbal adjuncts whose understood subject is the speaker ([23], p. 611) could support the verb analysis of assuming, but it doesn’t reconcile Ch. 8 with Ch. 11’s listing of supposing. Ch. 7’s list also omits two items that Ch. 11 lists.
inference: Is supposing a verb or a preposition when it takes a content clause?

evidence.passage: §14.4, p. 758. “Assuming and supposing are verbs heading gerund-participial clauses.”
evidence.establishes: Chapters 8 and 11 assign supposing to different categories in the same construction.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
